read with the Rules and the MCA Circulars, are appended below.

read with the Rules and the MCA Circulars, the manner of voting on the proposed Resolution is restricted only to remote e-voting
(“e-voting”) i.e. by casting votes electronically instead of submitting postal ballot forms. The instructions for e-voting are appended
to this Postal Ballot Notice.
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its Meeting held on April 30, 2026, have appointed Mr. Suresh Viswanathan, Designated
Partner, M/s. SVVS & Associates Company Secretaries LLP, Practicing Company Secretaries, as the Scrutinizer(s) for conducting the

Ballot shall be final.

Notice are requested to carefully read the instructions mentioned under the head ‘Instructions for e-voting’ in this Postal Ballot Notice
and record their assent (“FOR”) or dissent (“AGAINST”) on the proposed Resolution.

1. Purpose and Scope

Edelweiss Financial Services Limited and its subsidiaries, associates, and group entities in India and overseas (collectively
referred to as ‘Edelweiss’) are committed to the confidentiality, privacy, security and protection of PII (as defined below)
collected from/ disclosed by/ shared by Data Subjects (as defined below) including its employees (at all levels and grades,
whether regular, fixed-term contract or temporary), contractors, vendors, associates, consultants, customers and business
partners of Edelweiss.

This Privacy Policy (hereinafter referred to as ‘Policy’) broadly outlines the security and privacy practices and procedures
adopted by Edelweiss for collection, receipt, possession, storage, dealing, handling, processing and protection of Personal
Data (as defined below) are hereinafter collectively referred to as PII of the Data Subjects, in compliance with applicable
laws and regulations.

This Policy is applicable to (i) all Data Subjects who provide, disclose, and share PII with Edelweiss, (ii) Data Processors (as
defined below) working with or for Edelweiss, and who have or may have access to or receive PII from Edelweiss and who
have access to PII collected or processed by Edelweiss; and (iii) Data Controller Employees of Edelweiss who have access to
PII collected or processed by or on behalf of Edelweiss.

The Data Subjects, Data Controller and the Data Processors are expected to read, understand and comply with the Policy.

This Policy applies to all information that Edelweiss Financial Services Limited and all its group entities collectively referred
to as Edelweiss collect, use, process, store, share and dispose personally identifiable information (PII) from the access made
to websites, and provision of products & services.

2. Applicable Laws, Rules and Regulations:
   Edelweiss’ obligations in connection with data privacy presently emanate from:

        •   The Information Technology Act, 2000;
        •   The Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or
            Information) Rules, 2011.
        •   Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023;
        •   Any other applicable laws, rules, regulations, enactments introduced from time to time.

3. Data subject’s rights:

A Data Subject may request a report of the PII Edelweiss holds and can ask to review, correct, verify, delete, or erase that
data by contacting the Data Privacy Officer using the provided details. The Data Subject must also inform Edelweiss of any
changes to their personal information during employment, contract, or business relationships. In the event of the death or
incapacity of the Data Principal, he/ she may nominate an individual who shall be entitled to exercise her rights on her
behalf.

Rights provided by DPDP Act:

    •   Right to access information about personal data.
    •   Right to correction and erasure of personal data
    •   Right of grievance redressal.
    •   Right to nominate.

4. Edelweiss commits towards:

•   Collection of PII

Edelweiss collects data subjects’ PII only for specific, explicit, contractual, regulatory, or other legitimate purposes,
complying with all applicable laws. It may receive PII from third parties (e.g., recruiters or websites) under the same legal
standards, though it is not liable for those parties’ disclosures. The PII is combined with other data to deliver and improve
services and is processed lawfully, adequately, relevantly, and solely to the extent necessary for business or legal obligations.
Edelweiss does not share PII with external parties except when required to meet statutory or contractual requirements.
 •   Data protection

Edelweiss is dedicated to safeguarding the personally identifiable information (PII) of its customers, users, and employees,
and it actively honours their preferences on how that data is used. Its privacy policy applies universally, recognizing that
protecting user privacy and security is an inherent responsibility of delivering products and services to all. Edelweiss
ensures that data handling practices, technologies and personnel keep user data private, safe, and secure, and it commits
to continuously enhancing its level of protection.

•   Processing and transfer of PII

Edelweiss will not knowingly gather / process PII from children or minors without prior parental consent where required
by law. In case the Data Principal does not agree with the policy and objects to the processing of PII required for legitimate
purposes, they must immediately cease using Edelweiss’ services and notify the Data Privacy Officer in writing to withdraw
their consent.

Edelweiss may merge a Data principal’s PII with that of other users, then share only the resulting aggregated, fully
anonymized data with third parties such as investors, affiliates, partners, or advertisers. The anonymized data cannot
identify any individual and is disclosed solely in compliance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations—for example, to
report industry, marketing, or employment trends.

Additionally given that Edelweiss is an organization having an international presence by submitting PII, Data principals
agree to storing, processing, and transferring of the PII to location other than India. Moreover, it is clarified that whenever
Edelweiss shares data, it relies on lawful measures to transfer such data.

•   Disclosure of PII

Edelweiss may share / disclose Data Subjects’ PII only with vendors / data processors acting on its behalf for permitted
activities (e.g., design, testing, analytics, marketing) under strict policy instructions; it may also disclose PII during
corporate transactions (e.g., mergers, asset sales) with usage limits; it may reveal PII for legal reasons—such as
law-enforcement requests, court orders, or to prevent harm, investigate wrongdoing, enforce agreements, or protect its
services.
